b1-gan-participle.title: Experience/Result: -gan
b1-gan-participle.explanation: Uzbek has no separate present-perfect verb form the way English does ("have gone"); instead the participle -gan (voiced to -kan or -qan depending on the stem's last sound) plus a predicative ending covers both "has done X" and "did X, with present relevance": men bu filmni ko'rganman (I have seen this movie), u Parijga borgan (he/she has been to Paris).
b1-gan-participle.fact: The very same -gan form, without any predicative ending at all, also works as a plain adjective built from a verb: o'qigan kishi literally means "a person who has read/studied" -- i.e. an educated person -- one suffix covering both a full sentence and a single descriptive word.

dialogue.en: Have you been to this city?
Yes, I have been there twice.

b1-conditional.title: Conditional: -sa
b1-conditional.explanation: The conditional suffix -sa attaches directly to the verb stem, with the optional word agar ("if") added at the front for clarity: agar vaqtim bo'lsa, kelaman (if I have time, I'll come). The -sa clause always comes first, the result clause second.
b1-conditional.fact: Agar is genuinely optional -- vaqtim bo'lsa, kelaman means exactly the same thing without it -- because -sa alone already marks the clause as conditional; agar is there purely to flag the condition earlier for the listener, the way a comma-splice "if" softens a sentence in English but isn't grammatically required.

dialogue.native: Agar ertaga yomg'ir yog'sa, nima qilamiz?
dialogue.en: If it rains tomorrow, what will we do?
If it rains, we'll stay home.

b1-reported-speech.title: Reported Speech: deb
b1-reported-speech.explanation: Deb, a converb of demoq ("to say"), follows a quoted clause to mark it as reported speech or thought: Ertaga kelaman, deb aytdi (He/she said, "I will come tomorrow" / that he/she would come tomorrow). It can also report a belief or reason: kech qoldim, deb o'yladim (I thought I was late).
b1-reported-speech.fact: Deb is so productive it isn't limited to reporting speech at all -- it also marks the reason behind a naming or labeling, as in Toshkent, deb ataladi ("[it] is called Tashkent") -- the same tiny word bridges quotation, thought, and naming.

dialogue.en: He/she said that he/she would come tomorrow.

b1-concession.title: Concession: -sa ham / garchi
b1-concession.explanation: Adding ham ("also/even") after the conditional -sa turns "if" into "even if/although": yomg'ir yog'sa ham, boramiz (even if it rains, we'll go). Garchi ("although") can be added at the front for extra emphasis, but -sa ham alone already carries the full concessive meaning.
b1-concession.fact: This means Uzbek builds "although" out of the exact same conditional suffix used for plain "if" -- just by adding one small word, ham, after it -- rather than needing a completely different grammatical structure the way English switches from "if" to "although".

dialogue.en: Will you come even if you're tired?

dialogue.native: Ha, charchagan bo'lsam ham, albatta kelaman.
dialogue.en: Yes, even if I'm tired, I'll definitely come.

b1-passive.title: Passive Voice: -il / -in
b1-passive.explanation: The passive is formed by inserting -il (after most consonant-final stems) or -n (after vowel-final stems) between the verb stem and the tense ending: kitob o'qildi (the book was read), xat yozildi (the letter was written), eshik ochildi (the door was opened).
b1-passive.fact: Because the passive marker sits in the same slot as -a olmoq (ability) and -moqchi (intention), a single Uzbek verb stem can in principle carry several of these layered suffixes at once, each one shifting the meaning by a small, predictable step.

dialogue.en: It was written in the last century.

b1-digan.title: General Participle: -digan
b1-digan.explanation: -digan turns a verb into a description of habitual or general action, working much like an English relative clause: o'qiydigan kitob ("a book that is read/for reading"), ishlaydigan joy ("a place where one works", i.e. a workplace).
b1-digan.fact: Unlike -gan (a specific, completed action), -digan describes something general or repeated -- kelgan kishi is "the person who came [that one time]", while keladigan kishi is "the person who [regularly/is going to] come" -- the same root, two different suffixes, two clearly different meanings.

dialogue.en: Are there any books to read here?

dialogue.native: Ha, javonda ko'p qiziqarli kitoblar bor.
dialogue.en: Yes, there are many interesting books on the shelf.

items.en: I have seen this movie.
He/she has been to Paris.
Have you read this book?

items.uz: Biz bu masalani ko'p marta muhokama qilganmiz.
items.en: We have discussed this issue many times.

items.uz: U hech qachon Amerikaga borgan emas.
items.en: He/she has never been to America.
I have met this person before.
They have moved away from this city.
Have you tried this food?
I have heard this song before.

items.uz: U bu ishni bir necha marta bajargan.
items.en: He/she has done this job several times.

items.uz: Biz bu yerga kelganimizga uch yil bo'ldi.
items.en: It's been three years since we came here.
They have resolved this issue.
If I have time, I'll definitely come.
If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.

items.uz: Agar ko'p mashq qilsang, tez o'rganasan.
items.en: If you practice a lot, you'll learn quickly.

items.uz: Pul yetarli bo'lsa, uy sotib olamiz.
items.en: If we have enough money, we'll buy a house.
If he/she doesn't come, we'll start.
If I wake up early, I exercise.

items.uz: Agar imkoniyat bo'lsa, chet elga borardim.
items.en: If I had the opportunity, I would go abroad.
If you help, we'll finish faster.

items.uz: Agar bu ishni tugatsam, dam olaman.
items.en: If I finish this task, I'll rest.
If the weather is good, we'll go to the park.

items.uz: Agar siz istasangiz, men tushuntirib beraman.
items.en: If you want, I'll explain it.
If he/she comes, let me know.
He/she said that he/she would come tomorrow.
I thought I was late.

items.uz: U bu ishni bajaraman, deb va'da berdi.
items.en: He/she promised that he/she would do this task.
They believed they would win.

items.uz: U meni tushunmadi, deb xafa bo'ldi.
items.en: He/she got upset thinking that I didn't understand him/her.
My mother said we wouldn't go tomorrow.

items.uz: U bu joy juda go'zal, deb yozgan edi.
items.en: He/she had written that this place is very beautiful.
I consider this to be correct.
I thought he/she wanted to call me.
They were afraid they wouldn't make it in time.
This city is called beautiful.
I thought he/she didn't recognize me.
Even if it rains, we'll go.
Even though I'm tired, I'll finish my work.

items.uz: Garchi qiyin bo'lsa ham, u taslim bo'lmadi.
items.en: Although it was difficult, he/she didn't give up.

items.uz: Pulim kam bo'lsa ham, yordam berdim.
items.en: Even though I had little money, I helped.

items.uz: U kasal bo'lsa ham, ishga bordi.
items.en: Even though he/she was sick, he/she went to work.

items.uz: Vaqtim yo'q bo'lsa ham, kelishga harakat qilaman.
items.en: Even though I don't have time, I'll try to come.

items.uz: Garchi yosh bo'lsa ham, u juda aqlli.
items.en: Although he/she is young, he/she is very smart.

items.uz: Sovuq bo'lsa ham, bolalar tashqarida o'ynashdi.
items.en: Even though it was cold, the children played outside.

items.uz: Qiyin bo'lsa ham, men bu vazifani bajaraman.
items.en: Even if it's hard, I'll complete this task.

items.uz: U charchagan bo'lsa ham, jilmayib turardi.
items.en: Even though he/she was tired, he/she kept smiling.

items.uz: Garchi kech bo'lsa ham, u telefon qildi.
items.en: Although it was late, he/she called.

items.uz: Pul yo'q bo'lsa ham, biz baxtlimiz.
items.en: Even without money, we are happy.
This book was written last year.
The door was opened by someone.

items.uz: Bu uy o'n yil oldin qurilgan.
items.en: This house was built ten years ago.
The letter has already been sent.
This issue has not yet been resolved.
A new law was adopted.

items.uz: Bu taom maxsus retsept bo'yicha tayyorlanadi.
items.en: This dish is prepared according to a special recipe.
The project was successfully completed.
These words will never be forgotten.

items.uz: Kitob bir necha tilga tarjima qilingan.
items.en: The book has been translated into several languages.
This building was renovated.
All documents were checked.
Is there a place to study here?
I need a pen to write with.
Is this drinking water?
The company where he/she works is very big.
I don't have clothes to wear.
What is your favorite food (the food you love)?
This is the place where we live.
The playing children are on the street.
The expected result will be good.
This product that's being sold is very popular.
I have many books to read.
This road that leads there is very long.
